text: Baleka Mbete, born on 24 September 1949 in Clermont, a township in Durban, KwaZulu-Natal, to a Hlubi family, is a South African politician who served as Deputy President of South Africa from September 2008 to May 2009. She was the Speaker of the National Assembly for two non-consecutive terms: from 2004 to 2008 and from 2014 to 2019, and served as Deputy Speaker between 1996 and 2004. A member of the African National Congress (ANC) since 1976, she was first elected to the National Assembly in the first post-apartheid elections in 1994 and held the seat until 2019, with a break from 2009 to 2014. She qualified as a teacher in 1973 and taught in KwaMashu before becoming involved in the Black Consciousness Movement, which led to her detention in 1976. She left South Africa for Swaziland on 10 April 1976 and later moved to Tanzania, where she worked with the ANC's Women's Section and headed the Medu Art Ensemble, also publishing poetry under her married name, Baleka Kgositsile. She returned to South Africa in June 1990 and participated in the negotiations to end apartheid, serving as secretary-general of the ANC Women's League from 1991 to 1993. In 1995, she was appointed chair of the ANC's parliamentary caucus and a member of the Presidential Panel on the Truth and Reconciliation Commission. In May 1996, she became Deputy Speaker, succeeding Bhadra Ranchod, and was re-elected to that office in June 1999. In April 2004, she was elected Speaker of the National Assembly unopposed, with Gwen Mahlangu as deputy. During her term, she faced criticism over the Travelgate scandal and the use of parliamentary travel vouchers, and in January 2006, she chartered a jet costing R471,900 to attend the inauguration of Ellen Johnson Sirleaf in Liberia. In December 2007, she won election as ANC national chairperson with 61% of the vote, defeating Joel Netshitenzhe, and served in that role until December 2017. On 25 September 2008, she was appointed Deputy President following the resignation of Thabo Mbeki, though she did not become President, as Kgalema Motlanthe was appointed to that role. In May 2009, she was re-elected to the National Assembly but declined to be sworn in, leading to her stepping back from Parliament. She returned in May 2014 as Speaker, defeating Nosimo Balindlela in a vote of 260 to 88, and faced a no-confidence motion in September 2014 that was rejected 234 to 0 after opposition parties walked out. She has faced accusations of bias toward the ANC and being a puppet of President Zuma, and in March 2016, the Constitutional Court ruled that the National Assembly under her leadership breached the Constitution by failing to implement the Public Protector's Nkandla report. In April 2016, she identified herself as a presidential contender, but endorsed Cyril Ramaphosa at the ANC's 54th National Conference in December 2017, after being disappointed that Jacob Zuma did not support her campaign. She did not run for re-election as national chairperson and was not re-elected to the National Executive Committee at the 2017 conference, though she remained a member until 2022. In May 2019, she was re-elected to her parliamentary seat but was subsequently removed from the party list, and the ANC announced Thandi Modise would succeed her as Speaker. In March 2022, she stated she was "done with politics," but was appointed interim convener of the ANC Women's League in September 2022, serving until a new leadership was elected. At the ANC's 55th National Conference in December 2022, she was not re-elected to the National Executive Committee, marking her first loss since 1994. Mbete has been linked to business ventures, including shares in Dyambu Holdings, which is involved in the Gautrain project and has ties to Brett Kebble, and was implicated in a R25 million Gold Fields bribe in 2010. She married Keorapetse Kgositsile in 1978, divorced in 1992, and remarried Nape Khomo in 2016. She has three sons and two daughters.
